newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA TO EXPORT 30,000 TONNES OF COOKING OIL.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA TO EXPORT 30,000 TONNES OF COOKING OIL.

text.p: Bulgaria's cabinet on Thursday lifted a ban on exports of 30,000 tonnes of cooking oil in a bid to raise funds needed for wheat imports, Agriculture Minister Krastyo Trendafilov said.
"We plan to export 30,000 tonnes of cooking oil so we can procure additional funds for wheat imports," he told reporters after a cabinet meeting.
Sunflower oil exports will be charged with an export fee of $100 per tonne, Trendafilov said.
Oil producers are expected to receive commercial bank loans worth some 4.2 billion levs to boost their output, Trendafilov said.
The decision comes into force 14 days after being published in the State Gazette.

Bulgaria, hit by unprecedented grain shortage due to excessive exports last year and bad harvest this year, said it will import 1.6 million tonnes of grain to guarantee human and animal wheat and fodder consumption. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
